overall: The AG found the Swansea School Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law on any of three allegations: meeting recording notice, approval of minutes by consent agenda, and a chair's reply-all email.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Chair did not announce that the complainant and two reporters were recording the June 23 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Chair met his obligation at the beginning of the meeting to "inform other attendees of any such recordings" and did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee did not formally accept prior minutes but approved them through a consent agenda at the June 23 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find this to be an acceptable method of approving meeting minutes, thus the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Chair's July 9 reply-all email to the complainant, sent to a quorum of the Committee, was improper deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: Although the communication concerned a matter within the Committee's jurisdiction and reached a quorum of its members, because the members were not the intended recipients we find there was no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
